components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Quieter sibling to the primary. Carries secondary actions on the same surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: #ffffff; color: #4a4a4a; font-family: 'Geist', -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid #e8e6e0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f0eee9; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1a1a1a; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Decodable is software that feels like a tutor's actual notebook: warm paper, ink, ruled lines, and the same patient density a working tutor builds up across a year of sessions. Every screen is a page you'd be proud to leave open on a desk during a parent meeting. The aesthetic prioritizes calm over excitement; the user is a teacher doing careful work for a child, not a power user grinding through tickets.

Density is high but never crowded. Information lives in ruled tables, eyebrow labels, and short titled paragraphs rather than tiles and metric heroes. Color is restrained and warm. Type carries most of the hierarchy. Surfaces are flat: depth comes from ink weight, rule lines, and rhythm, not shadows.

This system explicitly rejects four families: kid-coded edtech, SaaS dashboard cliché, clinical software, and creator-tool maximalism. Decodable is for an adult professional, in daylight, with kindness in the voice.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white paper (#f5f3ef) is the dominant surface, never pure white as the background.
Ink-on-paper contrast (#1a1a1a on #ffffff cards) carries primary affordances.
Status color appears only when it earns it: a tag, a dot, a banner. Not as decoration.
Geist (sans) carries body and UI; Geist Mono carries data, IDs, and dates.
Flat by default. No shadows on rest state. Hover lifts via background tint, not elevation.

rules.name: The Ink-Carries-Action Rule
rules.body: Primary action color is ink, not purple, not green, not blue. If a button needs attention, ink-on-paper is the strongest signal in the system; reach for color only when ink is already in use nearby.

rules.name: The Tint-or-Solid Rule
rules.body: Status colors appear as a saturated solid (dot, icon) OR as a -tint background carrying its same-hue solid text. Never as a saturated background carrying white text in product UI.

rules.name: The Pure-Black Prohibition
rules.body: Never #000. Hover state on the primary button is the only place black appears.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every panel section in the right sidebar leads with an uppercase 11px label at 0.6px tracking. Removing the eyebrow flattens the rhythm.

rules.name: The Tracking-Tightens-As-Size-Grows Rule
rules.body: Body and small sizes use normal tracking. The 22px display tightens to -0.5px.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, list rows, modals, and panels carry no shadow at rest. If a surface needs to read as primary, increase its ink content or thicken its border, do not float it.

rules.name: The Hover-Tints-Don't-Lift Rule
rules.body: Hover state on rows and cards swaps the background from paper-surface to paper-surface-2. Never transform: translateY(). Never a shadow ramp.

dos: Do lead each panel section with an 11px uppercase 0.6px-tracked eyebrow label.
Do use #1a1a1a ink on #ffffff cards, on #f5f3ef paper.
Do carry hover state by swapping paper-surface ↔ paper-surface-2.
Do use Geist Mono for dates, IDs, tutor names in tables.
Do keep status color rare. A row that uses no color is the norm.
Do prefer ruled list rows for showing many things. Cards are for one thing at a time.
donts: Don't ship a Duolingo-style edtech aesthetic: lime greens, cartoon mascots, gamification badges, gradient buttons.
Don't ship a SaaS dashboard cliché: purple-to-blue gradients, hero metric tiles, identical card grids.
Don't ship a clinical / medical look: sterile pure-white background, teal accent strips.
Don't ship a creator-tool look: dark mode, neon accents, complex panels.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use background-clip: text gradient text.
Don't add box-shadow to cards or rows.
Don't use transform: translateY() on hover.
Don't introduce a new accent color outside the six semantic colors.
Don't use em dashes in UI copy.
Don't wrap everything in a card.
